messages:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: P0 alert — service="inference-gateway-apac" — 5xx rate spike to 14% (baseline <0.5%) detected 2045678880s. Trigger: 3 consecutive 3m windows. Paging on-call. Investigate latency/5xx and rolling deploys.

alee: acked. I'm on it. pulling up dashboards now — linking metrics: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/inf/apac-errors?t=now-1h

morgan: i'm the release owner for the APAC blue/green. We started traffic shift at ~2045678600, weight -> green 80%. No canary errors in prod staging.

samir: seeing a weird mix — some clients resolving api.apac.redwood.com -> EU gcloud IPs, others to APAC green endpoints. probable DNS weighting mismatch or propagation TTL issue. grabbing dig output.

samir: ```
$ dig +short api.apac.redwood.com @8.8.8.8
34.120.12.34
34.120.56.78
35.187.200.10
# 2 of these are EU addresses (35.187.x.x), 1 is APAC (34.120.x.x)
```

alee: also seeing increased 502/504 from edge logs. snippet from edge logs: ```
[2045678802] upstream connect error: connection reset by peer for backend green-01.apac
[2045678810] 502 response from backend green-02 (timeout 3s)
```

morgan: oh—we enabled feature-flag `edge-route-v2` scoped to apac to route to the green service. That flag flip was behind the rollout. I validated at ~2045678605 but maybe scope mismatch.

irina: paging in SRE. hypothesis: DNS weight records for apac were updated, but a subset of resolvers still have cached EU answers due to TTL clash on prior records + LB health checks causing origin removal. Also CDN caches might be holding old clients to the wrong origin.

support-ash: Customer impact: Support tickets spiking for customers in APAC complaining about timeouts and 502s. I have a list of affected orgs in #support-alerts. Not a global outage but several enterprise requests degraded.

alee: action list proposed:
1) flip feature-flag `edge-route-v2` -> off (kill-switch)
2) rollback green deployment if necessary
3) purge CDN / edge caches for api.apac
4) update DNS TTL short-term and reconcile record weights
I'll take 1 and 3. Morgan please confirm 2 if kill-switch doesn't stabilize.

morgan: agreed, do the kill-switch. I'll stand by for rollback.

alee: running ffctl now `ffctl set edge-route-v2 off --scope region:apac --reason "emergency kill-switch 5xx spike"`

pagerduty-bot: Audit: feature-flag edge-route-v2 set to OFF by alee at 2045678923.

samir: kill-switch propagated to our conf-store, but I'm still seeing mixed resolution from global resolvers. TTLs on the DNS records were 300s but some caches showed older values; also the weighted LB removed some blue endpoints because of health-check flapping earlier — that explains the EU IPs.

alee: purging CDN for api.apac redwood paths now: `cdnctl purge --zone apac --path /v1/*` — started at 2045678950.

devops: triggered immediate purge; edge purge job id: purge-2045678952. ETA ~30s.

support-ash: customer channels notified: emails + status page update drafted. No public incident page yet, keeping targeted comms to affected customers.

alee: status update: after flag off + purge, 5xx rate dropped from 14% -> 6% in 2m but still above baseline. Some clients still timing out (likely cached DNS).

morgan: I'm going to roll back the green deployment to blue entirely for APAC. Executing k8s rollout undo for service `inference-apac-green` — will cut traffic back to stable.

morgan: ```
kubectl -n inference rollout undo deployment/inference-apac-green --to-revision=2
kubectl -n inference set image deployment/inference-apac-blue inference=registry.redwood/inference:stable-20260201
```

pagerduty-bot: CLI action noticed: rollback started by morgan at 2045678990.

alee: after rollback completed (2045679020) 5xx rate is down to 1.1%. Latency normalized. Edge errors dropped to baseline.

irina: followups to capture in postmortem:
- root cause: combination of health-check flapping on blue endpoints + DNS weighted update created mixed resolver state, exposing clients to unhealthy green backends. Feature-flag kill-switch helped but DNS TTL + CDN caches caused residual impact.
- mitigation effectiveness: kill-switch + CDN purge gave partial recovery, full rollback required for complete stabilization.
- ops gap: no short-circuit check to validate global DNS propagation during weighted DNS shifts; no automated traffic hold on >x% error rise during rollout.

product-ellen: noted customer impact. We should consider a guardrail: if error rate >1% during progressive rollout, automatically pause further weight increases and revert to previous weight. Also add canary-only health check that verifies edge success before weight changes propagate globally.

support-ash: collecting affected customer list and drafting incident comms for tomorrow. Will coordinate with legal for enterprise notifications.

morgan: will add stricter rollout checklist: verify LB health & DNS sanity across regions + perform staged TTL bump before traffic shift. Also will add explicit step to check CDN purge in parallel.

alee: handing off to the on-call for post-incident follow up. I'll create the incident ticket and postmortem template: https://pm.redwood.internal/incidents/2045678910
If anything regresses ping @alee and escalate.

pagerduty-bot: Incident P0 acknowledged and transitioned to post-incident at 2045679375 by alee.

support-ash: noted. closing the customer hotfix channel; follow-ups scheduled at 10:00 local tomorrow.

morgan: thanks team. Good recovery. We'll schedule a retro and the rollout checklist update. :thumbsup:
